reuse.why: Implements the daily-skip rule inline in getNextDate instead of in the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend that all weekend-handling sites call, and reads schedule.data.frequency without extending parseRecurDate, which builds that data.

duplication.why: The diff itself adds no copied block, but it hand-codes a separate weekend predicate (filter on d.isWeekend) and an extra skipWeekend/noSkipWeekend condition next to the existing one.

placement.why: The rule lands in one consumer (getNextDate) rather than in the shared weekend definition, so getUpcomingDates and the budget schedule template still apply the old move rule to daily schedules.

scope.why: Small and focused on the request, with tests.

maintainability.why: Weekend behaviour now differs by call path, the enable condition is evaluated in two shapes in the same function, and the daily check depends on a data field the parser never sets.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate in shared/schedules.ts decides the daily-weekend rule itself instead of through getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and relies on schedule.data.frequency without adding it in parseRecurDate (rules/rule-utils.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: getNextDate re-expresses the weekend decision (skipWeekend && !noSkipWeekend, plus its own isWeekend filter) beside the existing skip call rather than extending the shared helper.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule exists only in getNextDate; getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) still call getDateWithSkippedWeekend with the old move rule.
